archetype: Mono-black aristocrats-combo: a sacrifice engine that draws while it assembles and closes with one of six rules-verified drain lines — two unbounded, one mandatory and finite-but-lethal, two library-bounded, and one rotation-engine primary that is measured rather than argued.

role_assignment.default_role: THE QUIET COMBO DECK — control posture, combo clock, and a commander who is both the draw engine and, for half the kill suite, the gate. Duke's operational test in strategy:whos-the-beatdown is 'who has inevitability? — whoever loses the long game must be the beatdown', and in a fair pod that is you: an ability reading 'Pay 1 life, Sacrifice another creature: Put a -1/-1 counter on up to one target creature and draw a card' (cards.json) costs no mana and turns every spare body into a card, and strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock's Commander correction is that 'four-player games trend long, so inevitability compounds — engines are the default winning plan'. The plan is assembly. strategy:critical-mass names the shape and its price — 'linear strategies give up flexibility in exchange for power', so 'the deck's defense is speed, redundancy, and resilience, not answers' — and the artifacts measure both halves of that sentence: the redundancy is real at every enabler layer (goldfish_metrics.json, 10,000 iterations, seed 42, unassisted / tutor-assisted by turn 10: a drain 82.3% / 93.6%, renewable fodder 82.3% / 93.3%, a free repeatable outlet 78.5% / 92.5%, an ignition source 73.8% / 90.2%, engine mana 61.2% / 85.8%, a tutor 61.2%), while the flexibility given up is the diagnosis's binding axis — 2 of 5 interaction classes covered, zero artifact answers by oracle enumeration over all 80 entries. The commander lands turn 4 in 7,188 of 10,000 games (mean 4.301, 91% by turn 6, turn 2 in 7.2% off the three-card fast-mana class). Sit under the radar and look like a value deck, but expect the read: strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection is blunt that 'combo decks look non-threatening while advancing in secret, which is exactly why experienced tables hit the quiet ramp player'. One discipline the split kill suite imposes: three of the six declared kills (D, E, F — including the primary) hold Yawgmoth in their verified scenarios and carry commander:true in goldfish_targets.json, so he is NOT a free lightning rod. In the grind phase trade him away cheerfully — he recasts from the zone and strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance prices 'one recast of a cheap commander' as a fine rate — but on the engine turn he is the hub, and by that section's own test ('how critical is the commander to the plan') the hub 'justifies constant protection down plus a held response on the pivot turn'. The deck holds exactly three cards that do that job (Lightning Greaves, Supernatural Stamina, Malakir Rebirth); hold them for that turn, not for value. Role stays seat-relative (strategy:whos-the-beatdown): control against fair midrange, the beatdown against any deck whose lock or clock arrives before your assembly (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial).
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: ONE ASSEMBLY IS THE TABLE — every verified kill ends all opponents, not a seat — so the go decision is a configuration check plus an interaction count, never body arithmetic. CONFIGURATION: six verified shapes. Unbounded, a decision you make once: Warren Soultrader + Gravecrawler + an each-opponent drain (stack 009, 'each activation's Treasure exactly funds the next cast'); Gravecrawler + Phyrexian Altar + a second Zombie + a drain (stack 011, 'the board returns to an identical state, so the loop is unbounded', ending at 80 life). Mandatory and finite-but-lethal: Exquisite Blood + a body reading 'Whenever you gain life, each opponent loses 1 life' (stack 012 — drain #40 takes every opponent from 1 to 0 simultaneously; the checker settled it is a win, not the 104.4b draw). Counted, arithmetic you must do at the table: Mikaeus + Yawgmoth + a non-Human body + a drain (stack 010 — 39 further activations against 59 the library permits, margin 20-25); Butcher Ghoul + Geralf's Messenger + a drain under Yawgmoth (stack 014 — library-bounded at ~55 activations because the draw is mandatory, lethal at ~30: each opponent loses 2 per two-activation cycle, the Messenger-targeted seat 4, pod 8, pilot net 0 life and 2 draws). Accumulated, the primary: Nest of Scarabs + any of nine drains with Yawgmoth from the zone (stacks 002/003/004 — one rotation is bounded by body exhaustion at 5-8 activations, roughly two drains per body, so the kill is rotations stacked across turns, not one loop). INTERACTION: strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window sets the bar the table applies — 'does this card win the game if it resolves' — and instructs you to 'assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing', preferring 'win attempts that leave a rebuilt position if they fail'. 009 is life-neutral, 011 pays nothing, 014 nets zero — cheap attempts by that standard. Sequence the drain last: it is the piece that reveals the plan, and strategy:tempo.sequencing's Commander correction — commit 'at the end step before your own turn so the table's chances to respond are spent' — is the default for deploying it.

engines.engine: THE PRIMARY KILL'S ENGINE — 'Whenever you put one or more -1/-1 counters on a creature, create that many 1/1 black Insect creature tokens' converts every commander activation into a body, and the body back into an activation. KILL E (Nest + any of nine drains, Yawgmoth from the zone) is the deck's best-measured line by a wide margin: 13.5% unassisted / 58.8% assisted assembled, 7.5% / 38.9% by turn 6, mean turn 6.267. Its arithmetic is settled twice over: one rotation exhausts its own bodies at 5-8 activations (stacks 002, 005), and the trigger counts are exact — one proliferate across three counter-bearing creatures makes three Insects, not four and not six (stack 013). Pilot it as rotations stacked across turns: each rotation is ~two drains per body across nine possible drains, and the table's life goes down in installments, not at once.
engines.evidence: verified stacks 002, 003, 004 (checker pass, Yawgmoth in each scenario); goldfish_metrics.json KILL E 0.135/0.588 assembled, 0.075/0.389 by turn 6; stacks 005 and 013 for the bounds and the token count

engines.engine: THE GATE AND THE DRAW ENGINE — a mana-free, instant-speed sacrifice outlet stapled to mandatory card draw, and the declared gate on three of six kills (D, E, F carry commander:true). The draw is the deck's real selection engine and it is UNMODELED: the goldfish's stated assumptions exclude extra card draw, so every unassisted rate is a floor on games where he sticks and digs. The same mandatory draw is also what bounds two kills — stacks 010 and 014 both terminate on the library because 'and draw a card' contains no 'may'. Use him to dig for three or four turns before using him for anything else; accept trades in the grind phase (he recasts from the zone); protect him only on the engine turn.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); goldfish_targets.json commander:true on KILL D/E/F; goldfish_metrics.json model_assumptions ('extra card draw... not modeled'); verified stacks 010 and 014 (mandatory draw sets the bound)

engines.engine: THE SELF-FUNDING RECURSION LOOP — its own ability modifies the zone it can be cast from, so with any other Zombie on board it recasts itself every iteration; pair it with a sacrifice-to-mana piece and an each-opponent drain and the loop pays for its own next cast. Two verified configurations: Warren Soultrader (Treasure) and Phyrexian Altar ({B} directly, a mana ability that 'never used the stack (605.3b)'). The deck's thinnest engine component by measured rate: one named card, 17.0% unassisted / 66.9% assisted by turn 10, both unbounded kills routed through it, and the skeptic-verified finding that no in-format lookalike substitutes.
engines.evidence: verified stacks 009 and 011 (checker pass); goldfish_metrics.json 0.170/0.669; diagnosis.json single_points_of_failure (Nether Traitor and Forsaken Miner refuted as substitutes from oracle text)

engines.engine: THE UNDYING PAIR — with Geralf's Messenger under Yawgmoth, alternating activations that sacrifice whichever undying body is counter-free while the -1/-1 counter strips the other's +1/+1. Verified library-bounded, NOT unbounded: the mandatory draw caps the loop at ~55 activations (~27 full cycles), and it is lethal at ~30 — each opponent loses 2 per two-activation cycle via a death drain, the Messenger's enters-trigger seat loses 4, pod total 8, pilot net 0 life and 2 draws per cycle, ~25 draws of margin inside the bound. The mechanism that sustains it is the counter-stripping: a creature that dies WITH a +1/+1 counter fails undying's intervening 'if' and never triggers at all.
engines.evidence: verified stack 014 (checker pass, iteration 1; independent simulation confirmed the 30-activation lethality with seats at exactly 0); goldfish_metrics.json KILL F 0.018/0.269 assembled

engines.engine: THE DRAIN THE VERIFIED BOARDS RESOLVED WITH — 'Whenever a creature you control dies, each opponent loses 1 life and you gain 1 life' (cards.json) is named in five checker-passed scenarios (002, 004, 009, 010, 011), second only to Nest of Scarabs. As a CLASS the drain layer is nine cards deep (Zulaport Cutthroat, Blood Artist, Ayara, Mirkwood Bats, South Wind Avatar, Marauding Blight-Priest, Starscape Cleric, The Meathook Massacre) at 82.3% drawn by turn 10 and 72.0% by turn 6 — the deck's best-built layer, and the payoff every one of the six kills routes through.
engines.evidence: verified stacks 002, 004, 009, 010, 011; goldfish_metrics.json drain class 0.823/0.936, Bastion alone 0.178/0.672; diagnosis.json engine.components payoff count 9

engines.engine: THE MANDATORY TWO-CARD LOOP — the only kill needing no outlet, no recursion and no commander. 'Whenever an opponent loses life, you gain that much life' against a body reading 'Whenever you gain life, each opponent loses 1 life' alternates one drain per cycle; the checker settled that this is a win and not the CR 104.4b draw case because every iteration lowers every opponent's life. Three bodies carry the text (South Wind Avatar, Marauding Blight-Priest, Starscape Cleric), and it is the fastest-assembling kill by mean turn (5.085) and the second-best measured (6.6% / 42.6%).
engines.evidence: verified stack 012 ('the sequence is not one that could be repeated indefinitely (732.1b) and there is a way to stop (104.4b)'); goldfish_metrics.json KILL C 0.066/0.426, mean_turn 5.085

engines.engine: THE LIBRARY-BOUNDED ANNIHILATION LOOP — grants undying to non-Humans; the commander's -1/-1 counter annihilates undying's +1/+1 at the state-based-action check and re-arms the body, and the loop's own mandatory draw ends it: 39 further activations against 59 the library permits, margin 20-25 depending on finisher sacrifices. The only undying-GRANTER in the 99 — only Butcher Ghoul and Geralf's Messenger carry undying natively — so he and the undying pair are the deck's two routes into that mechanism.
engines.evidence: verified stack 010 ('a library-bounded loop, not an infinite combo'); goldfish_metrics.json KILL D 0.046/0.343; diagnosis.json single_points_of_failure on the undying routes

engines.engine: THE RENEWABLE FODDER LAYER — nine sources that replace their own bodies (Nest of Scarabs, Bitterblossom, Grave Titan, Sedgemoor Witch, Black Market Connections, Reassembling Skeleton, Gravecrawler, Ophiomancer, Pawn of Ulamog), drawn in 82.3% of games and by turn 6 in 72.2%, with mean bodies at turn 6 of 4.239. This is the grind game the deck actually plays most sessions: fodder into the commander's draw while the tutors find a kill half. Ophiomancer's upkeep Snake and Pawn of Ulamog's per-death Eldrazi Spawn are the class's only members that pay in the commander's own currency without costing a card.
engines.evidence: goldfish_metrics.json RENEWABLE FODDER 0.823/0.933, by-turn-6 0.722; metrics mean_bodies_by_turn[6] 4.239; diagnosis.json fodder component count 9

engines.engine: ENGINE MANA AND ITS THIN COUSIN — five cards convert a creature death into castable black (Phyrexian Altar, Pitiless Plunderer, Phyrexian Tower, Black Market Connections, Warren Soultrader; 61.2% by turn 10), which is what makes the recursion loops self-funding rather than merely free. Distinguish it from FAST mana: Sol Ring, Ancient Tomb and Dark Ritual are the whole turn-2-Yawgmoth class, and at 3 cards / 43.6% it is the smallest and lowest-rated multi-card engine component the audit prices — the deck's mana is engine-shaped, not acceleration-shaped.
engines.evidence: goldfish_metrics.json engine mana 0.612/0.858, fast mana 0.436/0.777; verified stack 011 (Altar's ability 'is a mana ability, so it never used the stack (605.3b)'); diagnosis.json fast-mana component reading

engines.engine: THE ASYMMETRY CONVERTER — 'Whenever a creature you control dies, each other player sacrifices a creature of their choice' turns the same activations that feed a drain into table-wide edicts, the shape strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry asks for: 'Your cards should do something to all three seats or win the game.' It is the deck's only repeatable answer to a creature it cannot target (sole removal:edict role in the 99) — and also its least evidenced four-drop: zero checker-passed scenarios name it and no declared kill includes it, which is why the diagnosis ranks it the natural cut for an artifact answer.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); card_roles.json sole removal:edict; diagnosis.json cut_candidates[0] (skeptic-verified: zero mentions across all stack files)

engines.engine: THE BREADTH SLOT AND THE BINDING AXIS — 'Destroy target creature or enchantment an opponent controls' is the deck's one answer to a noncreature permanent, at 17.1% unassisted / 67.1% with a tutor spent on defence instead of a kill half. strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite puts 'breadth before depth: three opponents mean every permanent type appears, so cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land — before doubling any'; the diagnosis reads 2 of 5, and the artifact class is zero by enumeration of all 80 entries' oracle text. The format's cheap hosers for exactly this deck — Grafdigger's Cage on the graveyard-casting and undying returns, Cursed Totem on the creature outlets and the commander himself — are artifacts.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); diagnosis.json interaction-breadth liability (artifact zero by enumeration, skeptic-confirmed independently); goldfish_metrics.json 0.171/0.671

engines.engine: THE DRAW LAYER, priced in life — with Black Market Connections, Skullclamp, Castle Locthwain, Plumb the Forbidden, Ayara and the commander. The taxonomy counts 5 card-advantage copies against a target of 10, and the audit's own probe names five more filed elsewhere, so the functional count is roughly ten. strategy:card-advantage's Commander correction is why this layer is a strength rather than a finding: 'engines that out-draw three players are the format's defining advantage'. strategy:life-as-resource prices the fuel: 'early points are cheap and late points are priceless' — and the verified loops refund it (011 ends at 80, 014 nets zero per cycle).
engines.evidence: diagnosis.json card-advantage axis (counted 5, probe names Yawgmoth, Ayara, Black Market Connections, Castle Locthwain, Plumb the Forbidden); verified stacks 011 and 014 life ledgers

candidate_missing_lines.title: The six kills under Grafdigger's Cage — which shapes survive the archetype's hoser
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Oracle reading: KILL A and B cast Gravecrawler from the graveyard every iteration, and KILL D and F return creature cards from the graveyard via undying — all four look Cage-shaped — while KILL C (no graveyard) and KILL E (tokens) appear to run through it untouched. The diagnosis raises this as an open question and nothing verified settles which half falls; the pilot instruction ('under hate, pivot to C or E') and the case for an artifact answer both hang on it.

candidate_missing_lines.title: The outlet class under Cursed Totem
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Five of the eight free outlets are creatures with activated abilities and the commander's own ability is one; on oracle reading a Totem leaves only the noncreature outlets (both Altars, Blasting Station). Whether any verified kill still assembles through that remainder is unresolved and decides whether the artifact-answer gap is about graveyard hate only or the outlet class too.

candidate_missing_lines.title: The Meathook Massacre as a substitute drain in the recursion loops
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Oracle text: 'Whenever a creature you control dies, each opponent loses 1 life' is the same trigger condition and each-opponent reach stack 011 verified on Bastion of Remembrance. If it substitutes, the drain slot of both unbounded kills widens from three cards to four; goldfish_targets.json counts it in the nine-card drain class but not in KILL A or B's any_of.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Exquisite Blood plus Marauding Blight-Priest or Starscape Cleric — KILL C's ignition without the Avatar
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Both read 'Whenever you gain life, each opponent loses 1 life' verbatim — the identical text stack 012 resolved on South Wind Avatar — and combo_details carries both pairings as bracket-3 infinites. The unresolved half is ignition: 012's board starts from the Avatar's own dies-trigger lifegain, and neither substitute gains life by itself, so the line needs an external first lifegain event the verified board did not require.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Mikaeus plus a free sacrifice outlet, without the commander
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: combo_details carries seven such two-card records, each tagged 'Infinite death triggers'. Both verified undying loops (stacks 010 and 014) sustain themselves ONLY because a -1/-1 counter strips the +1/+1 between deaths — 014 states outright that a creature dying WITH a +1/+1 counter fails undying's intervening 'if' and never triggers. On plain oracle reading the bare two-card records lack any counter-stripping, so this is the deck's largest block of unverified containment and the most likely to be refuted; eight of the eleven two-card infinites behind the bracket floor belong to this family.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Gravecrawler plus Phyrexian Altar as a literal two-card infinite
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: The deck's most popular containment record (60,592) and a bracket_report.json exhibit. Stack 011 verified the loop on a four-card board — Carrion Feeder as the Zombie satisfying Gravecrawler's 'you control a Zombie' cast condition, Bastion as the drain — so the bare pair appears short a piece; whether any two-card configuration exists is unresolved and the bracket driver rests on the record, not a resolution.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Pitiless Plunderer + Ashnod's Altar + Reassembling Skeleton — infinite mana with no drain attached
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: combo_details rates it 52,227 producing 'Infinite colorless mana' and 'Infinite death triggers'; every piece is in the 99 and the Skeleton returns itself for {1}{B}, so the mana half is plausible on oracle reading. The death-trigger half would make it a seventh kill the moment any of the nine drains is on board. It is counted as a kill nowhere and should not be until resolved.

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: A sweeper is a payoff, not a loss — the danger sits one permanent type higher. Nine cards read some form of 'a creature you control dies, each opponent loses life', so a wrath that empties your board pays you for every body it takes, and 30 creature copies plus Reassembling Skeleton and Gravecrawler make you the cheapest rebuilder at the table; strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math's Commander correction is the default anyway — 'assume the wrath — over a four-player game one is near-certain — so deploy in waves, hold a rebuild package'. The real exposure: every verified kill is a pile of PERMANENTS, and the loops route through noncreature ones — Bastion in three verified boards, Exquisite Blood and Phyrexian Altar in others — while the deck's protection effects all protect a creature, so the enchantment that closes the game cannot be saved and the answer to a resolved noncreature threat aimed back at you is one card (Feed the Swarm, 17.1% / 67.1%). strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite's 'breadth before depth' names it; strategy:resource-hedging's 'hedge from ahead, gamble from behind' is the posture — hold the drain until the turn it converts (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window).
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Split the matchup in two, because the deck is built for one half and helpless in the other. Against TAXES it is quietly excellent, and the evidence is verified rather than argued: the commander's ability costs no mana, stack 009's Treasure 'exactly funds the next cast', stack 011's Altar refunds its own {B} through a mana ability, stack 012's loop is mandatory and spends nothing, and stack 014 nets zero life per cycle — a Sphere effect halves a two-spell turn but does nothing to a loop already running, so recount your hand, not your board (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial). Against LOCK PERMANENTS it is the worst deck at the table: Grafdigger's Cage sits on the graveyard-casting and undying halves of the kill suite, Cursed Totem on the creature outlets and the commander himself, and the 99 contains zero artifact answers by enumeration. strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial forces the role — 'you rarely own the long game under an assembling lock, so you are the beatdown, racing the lock's completion' — and its discipline is the operative one: 'Name your outs early — the removal or velocity that breaks the piece that beats YOU, not the scariest piece.' Here the honest naming is that against the artifact class the out is speed, because no removal exists.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: You are the control seat. Three scalable wipes (Black Sun's Zenith, Soul Snuffers, The Meathook Massacre) all double as engine ignition so no sweeper slot is dead, 12 interaction copies sit 50% over Walser's floor, Grave Pact converts your own engine into table-wide edicts, and 30 creature copies chump or eat attackers. Life is not the pressure point it looks like: stack 011 ends the pilot at 80 life, stack 014 nets zero, and the costs run 1 per commander activation and 1 per Necropotence card — strategy:life-as-resource's frame, 'early points are cheap and late points are priceless', means spend freely on cards early and switch to defending 'one turn before it matters, not one after'. strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy sets the removal bar at 'ends the game or ends my deck's function', not 'looks scary' — and on the primary engine an opposing small creature is not even a threat: stacks 002 and 003 establish that a 2-toughness enemy body EXTENDS a Nest rotation by two activations, so point the commander's counters outward whenever a legal target exists.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: The worst seat: the deck cannot interact on the stack at all, and its own kill needs a board. Mono-black's answer set stops at permanents — Deadly Rollick is free with the commander out, and nothing in the 99 touches a spell. strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy's countervailing clause is operative: 'held answers rot — against combo, or lethal already on board, the last profitable moment is now' — spend removal on the enabler the moment it lands, and apply strategy:critical-mass in reverse: 'hit enablers, not payoffs'. Where you can race is assembly at instant speed: the commander's outlet works at instant speed and stack 012's loop ignites from a free outlet's activation, so the close does not need a sorcery-speed window once the permanents are down (whether a full assembly fits inside another player's turn is not verified and is not claimed). strategy:resource-hedging.playing-to-outs is the posture behind their clock: 'identify the card or event that saves you and play as if it's coming' — commit to the shape you can complete, not the one you prefer.
matchup_frames.vs_graveyard_hate: Named separately because the archetype's primary hoser splits this kill suite cleanly in half, on oracle reading: KILLs A and B cast Gravecrawler out of the graveyard every iteration and KILLs D and F run on undying returns from the graveyard, so a Rest in Peace effect or a Grafdigger's Cage appears to blank four of six shapes — while KILL C touches no graveyard at all and KILL E runs on freshly created tokens. The correct read under hate is therefore to abandon the recursion shapes entirely and assemble toward E (the best-measured line, 38.9% by turn 6 with a tutor) or C (the fastest, mean turn 5.085): strategy:resource-hedging.playing-to-outs — 'know what you can't beat and stop paying for it.' The Cage question is flagged as a scenario need rather than asserted; what IS certain is that the deck cannot remove the hate piece itself, because the artifact answer class is zero by enumeration.
matchup_frames.vs_the_removal_heavy_pod: The seat-relative read strategy:whos-the-beatdown demands, made concrete: against a table that trades removal early, deflect (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection) and grind — the fodder and drain layers are both 82.3%, mean bodies at turn 6 is 4.239, and every dead body is a card via the commander. The one discipline is the split the kill suite imposes: removal aimed at Yawgmoth in the grind phase is a trade you accept and recast through ({2} per prior cast, strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance's honest math — 'protection slots and held mana cost you every game, removal only costs you some'); the SAME removal on the declared engine turn undoes a commander-gated kill, so the three protection cards are engine-turn cards, and strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window's 'assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal' is the sequencing rule for when he must survive.

distribution_notes: 36 land copies at the floor of strategy:deckbuilding.ratios' 36-38 band, 42 total mana sources, two unconditional taplands, and B at 33 land + 8 nonland = 41 sources against a 36-source Karsten target for 76 pips across 55 cards (deck-facts, mana_analysis.json) — on-curve 0.869 on lands alone, 0.948 with rocks and dorks. The curve is 14 / 17 / 19 / 10 / 2 / 2 from one to six, modal 3 against the format's measured modal 2 (strategy:deckbuilding.curve), with nothing above six; the verified kills are cheap enough that the empty top end is slack, not a hole. Role coverage is 97.5% with only Plumb the Forbidden and Supernatural Stamina unclassified, and the histogram is the archetype's: threat:body 30, wincon:drain 12, sac-cost 12, value:etb 12, sac-outlet 9, threat:tokens 9, tutor:unrestricted 5, against removal totalling ~15 across five role classes. Three counts are floors by the audit's own probe notes — card-advantage reads 5 with the function visible on five more cards, protection reads 3 with two protectors filed elsewhere, interaction-breadth reads 2 from an oracle-text heuristic (Bojuka Bog covers graveyard once, invisibly) — and only the last is a real finding, because the artifact class is zero by enumeration, not by heuristic. The goldfish model's own conservatism matters here: extra card draw is unmodeled, so the commander's mandatory per-activation draw — the deck's actual selection engine once he sticks — sits outside every rate quoted, and unassisted figures are floors. On the combo layer: 39 contained lines, 11 two-card infinites, and deck-facts is unambiguous that 'None is verified: a line is fact only once a stack artifact carries checker.verdict == pass' — the verified count is six declared kills across eight kill-bearing stacks. The synergy graph places 73 of the deck's cards with 65 intra-deck edges, a global top-10 shortlist that cannot price fit inside this list. Reading note for anyone building on the stack set: twelve of the fourteen checker-passed stacks resolve boards drawn entirely from the 99; stacks 001 and 007 resolve a Blowfly Infestation board — rules findings about how a counter engine and a creation-metered drain behave, not lines this list can present.
overall_assessment: This is a combo deck wearing a value engine's clothes, and its evidence is six checker-passed kill shapes rather than a containment count — with the distribution of boundedness doing the strategic work. Two are unbounded (stack 009's self-funding Treasure loop; stack 011's Altar loop, ending at 80 life): decisions you make once. One is mandatory and finite-but-lethal (stack 012 — 'not one that could be repeated indefinitely (732.1b)', lethal precisely because it ends, drain #40 taking all opponents from 1 to 0 at one state-based check). Two are library-bounded because the commander's draw is mandatory: stack 010 with 39 activations needed against 59 permitted, and stack 014's undying pair, ~55 activations available and lethal at ~30 — 8 pod life per two-activation cycle at net-zero cost to the pilot. And one — the primary — is an accumulating engine: KILL E, Nest of Scarabs plus any of nine drains with Yawgmoth from the zone, whose single rotation is bounded by body exhaustion at 5-8 activations (~two drains per body) and whose lethality is rotations stacked across turns. Keep the taxonomy rather than flattening it: an unbounded loop is a decision, a library-bounded loop is arithmetic you count at the table, and an engine kill is a pace you maintain. The measured hierarchy is unambiguous about which game to play: KILL E assembles at 13.5% / 58.8% (7.5% / 38.9% by turn 6), KILL C at 6.6% / 42.6% and fastest (mean 5.085), and everything else in single digits unassisted — so sequence toward the engine, hold the flashier loops as opportunism, which is strategy:critical-mass.storm-math's own instruction: 'pace for the median, hold the ceiling as opportunism'. Two structural facts govern the piloting. First, the commander is the gate on half the suite: D, E and F carry commander:true, the E stacks each hold him in scenario, and yet A, B and C need him not at all — so strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance's test ('how critical is the commander to the plan') gets a split answer this deck must manage by phase: trade him freely in the grind (he recasts; the tax is {2} and a turn), protect him absolutely on the engine turn, with exactly three cards (Lightning Greaves, Supernatural Stamina, Malakir Rebirth) that do that job. strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection's distinction lands precisely: this list is built around its commander and — for three of six kills — genuinely not reliant on him. Second, the ratio of assembly to protection is the linear deck's stated price: strategy:critical-mass — 'linear strategies give up flexibility in exchange for power', defense is 'speed, redundancy, and resilience, not answers' — and the redundancy half is measured and good at every enabler layer (drain 82.3%, fodder 82.3%, outlet 78.5%, ignition 73.8%, engine mana 61.2%, all rising toward 90% assisted), while the flexibility half is the binding axis: 2 of 5 interaction classes, zero artifact answers by enumeration, in a format whose cheap hosers for exactly this deck (Grafdigger's Cage, Cursed Totem) are artifacts. The deck does not lose to a wrath — nine drains make a wrath a payment — it loses to a two-mana artifact it cannot touch, or to graveyard hate that, on oracle reading, blanks four of six shapes while leaving the primary and the fastest intact. Tutors are the consistency layer, and their value is measured, not asserted: five tutors take the primary line from 7.5% to 38.9% by turn 6 — every kill's assisted rate is a multiple of its unassisted one — which is strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors' 'k tutors plus the card act like k+1 copies of every card' realized; spend them on kill halves, and remember the commander's own mandatory draw is a second, unmodeled selection engine on top. There is no honest union of six kill rates: the schema is an AND of ORs and cannot express one, and the kills share pieces (Gravecrawler in two, the drain class in nearly all), so adding double-counts and multiplying is wrong the other way. Quote the six per-kill rates; the count itself is the strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density statement — this is the median build the section endorses ('the ceiling build runs one spectacular finisher and loses when it's answered; the median runs three cheap ones and closes from any board'), with layered overlap ('overlap pieces, so five cards support four combos') taken further: nine drains support six lines. The bracket floor is 4, forced independently by four Game Changers and eleven two-card infinite records, and strategy:deckbuilding.power-level's Bracket 4 standard — 'lethal, consistent, and fast' — is met by verified lines, not argued from containment ('Contents give a floor, never a verdict'). Say it plainly at Rule 0: six rules-verified kill shapes, two unbounded, every one ending all opponents simultaneously. Then play it: deploy fodder and outlets early and cheaply, dig with the commander before you spend him, keep the drain in hand until the turn it converts, present at the end step before your own turn (strategy:tempo.sequencing), count the table's open mana (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window) — and go, because one assembly is not a seat. It is the table.
gaps: No aristocrats / sacrifice-loop section exists anywhere in the corpus. The outlet / fodder / payoff triad is this deck's entire architecture and the doc has no heading naming any of the three functions; a query for 'sacrifice outlet aristocrats engine' tops out near strategy:mulligans.engine-hands. It generalises to every Blood Artist and token-sacrifice deck in the format.

No vocabulary for what BOUNDS an iterative engine. This deck's checker findings draw the distinction three separate ways — bounded by the library because a draw is mandatory (stacks 010 and 014), bounded by bodies (stacks 002 and 005), and terminating only because the payoff is finite at 40 life per seat (stacks 009, 011, 012, where the checker needed CR 732.1b and 104.4b to separate 'unbounded' from 'mandatory but ending') — and the doc has no section in which 'library-bounded, lethal in ~30 with ~25 of margin' is even expressible. strategy:critical-mass.storm-math covers velocity and the go decision and never asks which resource runs out first.

No theory of trigger SURFACE — creation-side versus death-side payoffs. Stack 008 establishes that one commander activation paid with a token produces TWO triggers on a drain reading 'whenever you create or sacrifice a token' and one on a death-metered drain, because the sacrifice is a cost paid while the ability is on the stack. The distinction governs the median board and has no home in the doc.

strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors counts copies of an effect class with no notion that a RECURSIVE copy is worth more than a one-shot one. Gravecrawler is one card at 17.0% drawn by that arithmetic, and it is also the reason two kills are unbounded at all — the card recasts itself. Renewability belongs in that section's hypergeometric.

Nothing treats mana-free or self-funding kill lines as a class. The commander's ability costs no mana; stack 009 funds its own next cast; stack 011's mana ability refunds itself; stacks 012 and 014 spend nothing net. That is this deck's strongest property under taxes and it is verified — but strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial stops at 'recount your hand under the tax' and has no term for a kill that runs on zero external mana.

No theory for reading several partially-overlapping win conditions as one probability, and the artifacts cannot supply it either: goldfish's schema is an AND of ORs, so six kills carry six rates and their union has no expression. strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors does the hypergeometric for ONE effect class and strategy:combat-math.probability for one will-I-have-it question; neither says what to do with six correlated multi-card conjunctions. The honest discipline — name the count, quote each rate, decline to invent a seventh number — is one this deck supplies for itself.

No guidance for a SPLIT kill suite's commander insurance. strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance prices protection when the commander is the hub or when he is not; this deck is both at once — three kills gated on him including the primary, three needing him not at all, and the gate a timing tax on a commander who recasts from the zone. 'Protect by phase' (trade in the grind, insure on the engine turn) is the play the artifacts force, and no section expresses it.

No section on ANSWER-CLASS COVERAGE as a loss condition rather than a deckbuilding count. strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite lists the five classes and says cover them before doubling; it does not discuss being a combo deck whose own kill is a pile of permanents while holding zero answers to the class its hosers arrive in. The asymmetry — your kill is answerable by classes you cannot answer back — is this deck's binding axis and the corpus can only express half of it.
